scope: One-page curator-authorized follow-up: Finite Agency, Moral Demand, and Happiness.
approval: I approve a rewrite of 'Finite Agency' at your discetion.

source.title: Finite Agency, Moral Demand, and Happiness
prompts: Why can moral seriousness become psychologically extractive when responsibility is allowed to expand without limit?
What is scope leakage of happiness, and why is it a better name for a certain modern misery than vague burnout language?
How should a finite agent think about distant suffering without collapsing into either apathy or performative guilt?
Why might skepticism toward moral systems sometimes protect compassion rather than weaken it?

changes.changes: Explains the notice-to-duty-to-permanent-unhappiness inference; separates awareness, authorship, agency, blame and remedial reasons; retains the effective unlimited-mortgage passage; adds a hypothetical flood and warranted-sacrifice qualification.

Explains the proposed scope-leakage mechanism with the same flood example; removes unsupported diagnosis/cure and evolutionary-scale claims; distinguishes sorrow, exhaustion and a supposed obligation to remain unhappy; practical reach is not geographical proximity.

Develops the useful earlier stopping-rule example inside a complete response; specifies causal/role responsibilities, coordinated action, review triggers and costs; directly answers comfortable self-exemption and avoids inferring motives from public emotion.

Explains how guilt rituals displace attention to affected people; separates institutional contribution, power and cooperation; applies skepticism to both moral accusations and the critic’s excuses; preserves compassion without requiring moral realism.
